items.title: Frank Netto Interview, 1986-10-02
items.q: Uh, myself, Carl Martyr, Fisher, Steve Brew. ... I wanted to ask you about these kids that you taught in the Western Union Band. There was a boy, Martyr.

ctx.x: Never made a mistake, but he sounded like a, uh-oh, a saw.

I always kid him about it there. And there's Pinky Gerbrecht. You heard that name. Yeah. He's still there. And there's Maureen Lelke. And there's Leo Addy on drugs. Oh, yeah, that's him. Uh, myself, Carl Martyr, Fisher, Steve Brew. He's the only musician in W, uh, Op Union that died during the war. He went over to the, went over the top there, D-Day. Uh-huh. And then when he took a rest, they threw a bum in the, in the place where he was sleeping. Killed Steve. Frank Pinero. Uh-huh. And I don't know who else she…
No, that was a piano player.
No, what's his name? Carl Lelke. All right, now. And there was, his piano, his violin player was Carl Marder and his wife Maureen Lelke

That was the stringing song up there. And where was the picture taken? That's in WWL when it was in the Roosevelt radio station. And is it, did some of the guys double? It looks like it, looks like the Nina Pecone has a double. It looks like the Nina Pecone has a double. It looks like the Nina Pecone has a double.
